title: Leaf collapse retracts fixed-word tree zigzag categories
statement: Let $T$ be a small oriented tree: its underlying undirected graph is nonempty and has a unique finite simple path between any two vertices, and each edge is assigned one direction. Let $C_T$ be its free path category, whose arrows are finite composable directed edge words and whose identities are empty words. For a finite word $w$ in $+,-$, let $Z_w^{C_T}(x,y)$ have the meaning of [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus] for the pair $(C_T,C_T)$; identity horizontal arrows are allowed. Let $l$ be a leaf (a vertex incident to exactly one undirected edge), $a$ its neighbour, and $x,y$ vertices different from $l$. Put $T\prime=T\setminus\{l\}$, deleting also its incident edge. The inclusion $i:C_{T\prime}\to C_T$ and the functor $r:C_T\to C_{T\prime}$ sending $l$ to $a$, its incident edge to $1_a$, and all other vertices and generating edges to themselves induce functors $I_w:Z_w^{C_{T\prime}}(x,y)\to Z_w^{C_T}(x,y)$ and $R_w$ in the reverse direction. They satisfy $R_wI_w=1$. If the incident edge points $l\to a$, there is a natural transformation $1\Rightarrow I_wR_w$; if it points $a\to l$, there is a natural transformation $I_wR_w\Rightarrow1$. Its component at a zigzag has the incident edge at every occurrence of $l$ and identities at all other vertices; in particular its endpoint components are identities.

proof.text: Let $e$ be the unique edge incident to $l$. The inclusion of the graph of $T'$, fixing every vertex and edge of $T'$, extends uniquely to the free path functor $i:C_{T'}\to C_T$. The graph map sending $l$ to $a$, sending $e$ to the identity $1_a$, and fixing every other vertex and generating edge extends uniquely to a functor $r:C_T\to C_{T'}$: images of a directed edge word are obtained by replacing each occurrence of $e$ by $1_a$ and composing. Since $r$ fixes every generator in $C_{T'}$, the composite $r i$ is the identity functor.

source.place: Section 5.8(iii), printed p.25: finite-tree contraction by deleting a leaf; the fixed-word diagram-category formulation is expanded here.

proof.text: Apply $i$ and $r$ componentwise to the finite vertex-and-horizontal-arrow diagrams defining $Z_w^{C_{T'} }(x,y)$ and $Z_w^{C_T}(x,y)$, and apply them componentwise to commuting vertical diagrams. Functoriality preserves the prescribed direction of each horizontal arrow, commutativity, identities, and composition; because $x,y\ne l$ and both functors fix $T'$, endpoint components remain identities. This gives functors $I_w$ and $R_w$ in the stated directions. Applying $r i=1$ to every component gives $R_wI_w=1$ strictly, on objects and morphisms.

source.place: Section 5.8(iii), printed p.25: finite-tree contraction by deleting a leaf; the fixed-word diagram-category formulation is expanded here.

proof.text:
Suppose the incident edge is oriented $e:l	o a$. First, on $C_T$ itself, put $c_l=e:l	o a$ and $c_u=1_u$ for $u
e l$; we check $c_v\circ f=i r(f)\circ c_u$ for every arrow $f:u	o v$ of $C_T$. Since the only edge at $l$ leaves $l$, no nonidentity directed path ends at $l$ or passes through $l$. Hence there are three cases. (a) $u,v
e l$: $f$ avoids $l$, so $ir(f)=f$ and both sides equal $f$. (b) $u=l
e v$: $f=g\circ e$ with $g:a	o v$ avoiding $l$, so $ir(f)=g$ and both sides equal $g\circ e$. (c) $u=v=l$: the only arrow is $1_l$, $ir(1_l)=1_a$, and both sides equal $e$. The case $u
e l=v$ has no arrows. So $c:1_{C_T}\Rightarrow ir$ is a natural transformation. For a zigzag diagram $D$ in $Z_w^{C_T}(x,y)$, take the components $c_{D_j}$ at its vertices $D_j$. They are arrows of $C_T$, so they are allowed vertical arrows because the pair in [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus] is $(C_T,C_T)$, and the endpoint components are identities because $x,y
e l$. Every horizontal arrow of $D$, whether it is displayed rightward or leftward, is an arrow $f:u	o v$ of $C_T$, so the square above shows that these components form a commuting morphism $D	o I_wR_wD$. A morphism $\varphi:D	o D'$ consists of vertical arrows $\varphi_j:D_j	o D'_j$ of $C_T$, and the same square for $f=\varphi_j$ gives $I_wR_w(\varphi)\circ c_D=c_{D'}\circ\varphi$. This is the natural transformation $1\Rightarrow I_wR_w$.

source.place: Section 5.8(iii), printed p.25: finite-tree contraction by deleting a leaf; the fixed-word diagram-category formulation is expanded here.

proof.text:
Suppose instead that $e$ is oriented $a	o l$. On $C_T$ put $c_l=e:a	o l$ and $c_u=1_u$ for $u
e l$; we check $f\circ c_u=c_v\circ ir(f)$ for every arrow $f:u	o v$. Since the only edge at $l$ enters $l$, no nonidentity directed path starts at $l$ or passes through $l$. (a) $u,v
e l$: $f$ avoids $l$ and both sides equal $f$. (b) $u
e l=v$: $f=e\circ g$ with $g:u	o a$ avoiding $l$, $ir(f)=g$, and both sides equal $e\circ g$. (c) $u=v=l$: $f=1_l$, $ir(f)=1_a$, and both sides equal $e$. The case $u=l
e v$ has no arrows. So $c:ir\Rightarrow1_{C_T}$ is natural. As in the previous step, its components at the vertices of a zigzag $D$ are allowed vertical arrows with identity endpoint components, because $x,y
e l$. Applying the square to horizontal arrows of $D$, in either displayed direction, gives a morphism $I_wR_wD	o D$. Applying it to the vertical arrows of a morphism $D	o D'$ gives naturality in $D$. This gives the natural transformation $I_wR_w\Rightarrow1$.

source.place: Section 5.8(iii), printed p.25: finite-tree contraction by deleting a leaf; the fixed-word diagram-category formulation is expanded here.

proof.text: The constructions work for every finite signed word $w$, including the empty word and words with repeated vertices, because the component family is indexed by the finitely many diagram vertices and all checks are componentwise. Therefore the induced functors have the strict retraction $R_wI_w=1$ and the orientation-dependent natural transformation with the stated endpoint identities.
